source_admission: Sources read for the taxonomic system (taxonomy.md) and its register (taxa.py), 9 October 2026. 'access' records exactly what was read and how: 'online text' means the passage was read in the official online edition; 'abstract' means the PubMed or publisher abstract; 'record' means only the bibliographic record was confirmed (Crossref, PubMed or a registry). Passages from the codes are quoted or paraphrased by article number; no code text is copied into the repository. Translations from Classical Chinese, Latin, Greek and Old English in taxonomy.md are this work's, from the cited texts and dictionaries. Earth organisms the project's other studies already cite keep their sources in those studies' registers.

sources.citation: Turland, N.J., Wiersema, J.H., Barrie, F.R. et al. (eds) 2025. International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (Madrid Code). Regnum Vegetabile 162. Chicago: University of Chicago Press
sources.use: Botanical rules: independence, types, priority, a single correct name, names treated as Latin, retroactivity; ranks; generic names and epithets from any source; Latin or English diagnoses; preserved types; cultivated organisms; derogatory names; diacritics; etymology
sources.access: online text read: Principles I-VI; Preamble 8 and 11; Art. 3.1, 4.1-4.2, 8.1, 8.4, 13.1, 20.1, 23.1-23.2, 23.4, 28.1 with Notes 1-5, 29.1, 39.2, 42.1, 51.2, Rec. 51A.1, 60.7, Rec. 60I.1, 61.6; Art. 40 Ex. 10 (DNA sequences are not illustrations). Front matter and contents also read in the SANBI copy of the printed edition

sources.citation: Turland, N.J. 2025. From the Shenzhen Code to the Madrid Code: new rules and recommendations for naming algae, fungi, and plants. American Journal of Botany 112(4), e70026
sources.use: What changed at Madrid: voluntary registration of plant and algal names, rejection of derogatory names from 2026, the caffra epithets replaced, DNA-sequence types rejected and sent to a committee for 2029
sources.access: full text on PMC (PMC12012794), read through a summarizing fetch; the article numbers were then checked in the Code's online text

sources.citation: International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature 1999. International Code of Zoological Nomenclature, 4th edition, with the 2012 amendment on electronic publication and Declarations 44-47. London: International Trust for Zoological Nomenclature
sources.use: Zoological rules: scope and exclusions (names for hypothetical concepts are excluded), starting point 1758, binominal names, the Latin alphabet, derivation from any language, priority, electronic publication with ZooBank registration, the Code of Ethics
sources.access: online text read: Art. 1 (1.1-1.4 and Rec. 1A), Art. 3, Art. 5, Art. 8.5 (amended), Art. 11.2-11.3 and Rec. 11A, Art. 23.1, Appendix A, and the Glossary entry 'concept, hypothetical'

sources.citation: Oren, A., Arahal, D.R., Göker, M., Moore, E.R.B., Rossello-Mora, R. & Sutcliffe, I.C. 2023. International Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes. Prokaryotic Code (2022 Revision). International Journal of Systematic and Evolutionary Microbiology 73(5a), 005585
sources.use: Prokaryote rules: the nomenclature is not independent of the other codes, names are Latin and need an etymology, type strains deposited in two collections in different countries, strains and other infrasubspecific forms outside the Rules, Candidatus names without standing, sequence types rejected in 2020
sources.access: preprint text read: preface, General Consideration 7-8, Principles 1-9, Rules 5a-5d, 6 and 30, Appendix 10 (infrasubspecific subdivisions) and Appendix 11 (Candidatus). The published version was not re-read

sources.citation: Whitman, W.B., Chuvochina, M., Hedlund, B.P. et al. (eds) 2026. The Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes Described from Sequence Data (SeqCode), version 1.2.0, 12 August 2026
sources.use: Genome sequences as nomenclatural types, registration in the SeqCode Registry as a condition of valid publication, names unique against the other codes, roots from any language with the etymology given
sources.access: online text read: General Consideration 5; Principles 1-10; Rules 1, 8, 9a, 9b, Rec. 9, 16, 18a-18c, 26

sources.citation: Brickell, C.D., Alexander, C., Cubey, J.J., David, J.C., Hoffman, M.H.A., Leslie, A.C., Malécot, V. & Jin, X. (eds) 2016. International Code of Nomenclature for Cultivated Plants, ninth edition. Scripta Horticulturae 18. Leuven: ISHS
sources.use: Cultivars, Groups and grexes; genetically modified plants may form cultivars; cultivar epithets in living languages after 1958, at most 30 characters after 1995
sources.access: PDF from ISHS read: Preamble with its footnote on genetically modified plants, Principles 1-3, Art. 2.1-2.23, 3.1-3.3, 4.1-4.4, 21.11-21.14. No later edition was found

sources.citation: Cantino, P.D. & de Queiroz, K. 2020. International Code of Phylogenetic Nomenclature (PhyloCode), version 6. Ratified 20 January 2019 by the Committee on Phylogenetic Nomenclature; web version of 8 June 2020
sources.use: Clades named by phylogenetic definitions and registered; a clade is an ancestor and all its descendants; minimum-clade, directly-specified-ancestor, maximum-clade, apomorphy-based, crown and total (Pan-) definitions; names independent of rank; species names left to the rank-based codes

sources.access: API records read for every ranked backbone node (species/match) and for each candidate name (species?name=). The backbone gives no class for ray-finned fishes, so the register's run fish hang from Chordata through Salmonidae; it lists Cyanobacteria, where the ICNP name is Cyanobacteriota

sources.use: Life forms classed by where the surviving buds sit through the unfavourable season: phanerophytes, chamaephytes, hemicryptophytes, cryptophytes, therophytes; phanerophytes subdivided by height (nano under 2 m, micro 2-8, meso 8-30, mega over 30 m)
sources.access: OCR text read: pp. 15-19 (the five main types) and the table of phanerophyte heights

sources.citation: World Meteorological Organization 2017. International Cloud Atlas, section 2.1.3, Principles of cloud classification

sources.citation: Bosworth, J. & Toller, T.N. An Anglo-Saxon Dictionary, online edition
sources.use: Old English wolcen ('a cloud; the clouds; the heavens; the sky'), wolcen-faru ('the cloud-host, the moving clouds') and holm ('a mound, hill; wave, ocean, water, sea; land rising from the water, an island in a river')

sources.citation: Wiktionary, entries welkin, holm, sky, serene, wingu and mixtli (English edition), read 9 October 2026
sources.use: Secondary etymologies: welkin from Middle English welkne and Old English wolcnu; holm from Old English holm and Old Norse holmr 'islet'; sky from Old Norse sky 'cloud'; serene as a poetic noun and serene (serein) as fine rain from a cloudless sky after sunset; Swahili wingu, plural mawingu, 'cloud'; Classical Nahuatl mixtli 'cloud'
sources.access: entries read; their cited primary dictionaries (the Middle English Dictionary, the OED, Molina 1555) were not read here

sources.citation: Monier-Williams, M. 1899. A Sanskrit-English Dictionary. Oxford: Clarendon Press, p. 831 (Cologne Digital Sanskrit Dictionaries)
sources.use: megha, 'sprinkler', a cloud (from the root mih), also a mass or multitude; meghadūta, 'cloud-messenger', the name of a celebrated poem by Kālidāsa

sources.citation: Macdonell, A.A. 1911. Kālidāsa. Encyclopaedia Britannica, 11th edition, vol. 15, p. 668
sources.use: The Meghadūta describes the complaint of an exiled lover and the message he sends to his wife by a cloud

sources.citation: Zhuangzi, chapter 1, Xiaoyao you (逍遙遊), Chinese text
sources.use: The fish Kun of the northern darkness becomes the bird Peng, whose wings are like clouds hanging from the sky and which rises ninety thousand li; wind piled too thin cannot bear great wings. The phrase 去以六月息者也 is read either as resting after six months or as setting off on the sixth month's wind; taxonomy.md gives the first as one reading
sources.access: the opening passage read in the Chinese text; translations in taxonomy.md are this work's

sources.citation: Erya zhushu (爾雅注疏), juan 10, Shi yu, with Guo Pu's commentary (Siku quanshu text); and Yang Shen, Yiyu tuzan (異魚圖贊), juan 1, with commentary (Siku quanshu text)
sources.use: 鯤, 魚子: kun means fish roe, and Guo Pu glosses it as the young of all fish; the Yiyu tuzan commentary says that Zhuangzi made the smallest thing into the greatest
sources.access: the kun passages read in both texts on Wikisource

sources.citation: Lewis, C.T. & Short, C. 1879. A Latin Dictionary. Oxford: Clarendon Press (Perseus Digital Library)
sources.use: serenus 'clear, fair, bright, serene', of the sky (caelo sereno); nubivagus 'wandering among the clouds' (Silius Italicus 12.102); velivolus 'sail-flying', of the sea (Virgil, Aeneid 1.224); nubigena 'cloud-born', of the Centaurs and of Phrixus
sources.access: entries read: serenus, nubivagus, velivolus, nubigena
